findings.title: Additional CIQ parts: the supplier cannot report one as done and Beiersdorf cannot return it, because sections stay open until the final release
findings.claim: In v1, the supplier's only task for an additional part was the new CIQP Section item, and the query skipped 'Supplier: respond'. Under v2 the section item stays at 'Supplier: complete section' until PS-11, so this design breaks. The supplier has no native way to say the part is finished. The query sits at the department step from the moment it is raised. The department cannot return the part with a justification, because no supplier step lies on the query's path. The supplier's task also lacks a due date, a responsible person and a justification.
findings.evidence: portal-spec.mjs:123: 'Supplier: respond' runs only when Response_Required = "Yes". In the live draft, Response_Required is ReadOnly on every review step (none of those steps lists it as an override), so a department cannot switch a query to Yes later. Smoke test P3-skip-to-dept: a query with Response_Required = No goes straight from Start to 'Beiersdorf review - Safety', so its path is Start, then the department step, then End. portal-spec.mjs:99-103: P2 has a single supplier step and leaves it only when the supplier submits; the header at line 3 and the P2 description say sections stay editable until the final release. The traffic light in plan §6.1 line 493 ('amber once that item has ended') and the one-task design in §6.3 line 519 both assume the section item ends early, which v2 removes. The list value 'Additional part completed' (portal-spec.mjs:32) cannot be reached, because Response_Kind is set only at the skipped step. The live P2 field list has no Supplier_Due_Date, no Responsible_Name and no justification field. Untested: whether a contact listed in Assigned_Contacts can read a query that never reached a supplier step.
findings.recommended_fix: Raise additional-part queries with Response_Required = "Yes". The supplier then finishes the part by submitting 'Supplier: respond' with Response_Kind = 'Additional part completed'. The department can accept the part, or send it back with a justification, as in the normal loop. The supplier UI shows the query and the section as one task. Under v2 the section is a work area that stays open until the final release, so the query becomes the trackable task. If BDF insists on one native task, add Supplier_Due_Date, Responsible_Name and a request-justification field to P2 instead, and accept that the return path stays UI-only.

findings.title: The supplier can delete or change uploaded documents, and the upload date and uploader are values the supplier writes
findings.claim: v2 says documents are additive, suppliers cannot delete them, and each document is identified by file name and upload date. In the built model, uploads are rows of a child table that the supplier can fully edit, and the section stays at that step until PS-11. The supplier can therefore delete a row, replace the file, re-link it to another question, or change Upload_File_Name, Uploaded_At or Uploaded_By_Email. A query or assessment that references a document by file name and upload date (Ref_Doc_File_Name, Ref_Doc_Uploaded_At) can then point at nothing, or at a different file.
findings.evidence: portal-spec.mjs:96: the Uploads child holds Upload_File (Attachment), Upload_File_Name (Text), Uploaded_By_Email (Text) and Uploaded_At (DateTime). portal-spec.mjs:101 sets Uploads to Editable at 'Supplier: complete section'. In the live draft, Permission_16p9q4f sets the whole table column (Column_13ft021) to 'Editable'. That column has no add-only or no-delete setting, only AllowImport:false. master.md:403 lists the per-step states as Editable, ReadOnly, Hidden and Mandatory only. The 'rows are never deleted' rule (plan §4.2 line 218) is a convention, not something the platform enforces.
findings.recommended_fix: Record each upload as its own item that cannot be changed, for example a supplier-initiated 'CIQP Document' process whose Start submits straight to End. A smoke test already showed that an item with no matching step completes immediately (P3-invalid-dept). The upload date and uploader then come from the system fields _created_at and _created_by. After submit, only the admin delete route works (master.md:252). This is the fallback the plan already names for K-12. Keep Upload_Field_Key and Upload_Row_Id on that item. Have the internal session check _created_by against the case contacts, as the P4 integrity rule does. Before choosing, ask Kissflow product whether a table can allow adding rows but not deleting or editing them.

findings.title: A supplier edit after PS-05 creates no platform event, so re-derivation and informing departments cannot be automatic
findings.claim: v2 lets the supplier edit metadata, configuration answers and data directly until PS-11. It also says every change triggers an automatic re-derivation and informs the affected departments. In the built portal, these edits are field updates on a P2 item that stays at one supplier step. Kissflow integrations have no field-change trigger, and the supplier never writes to the app. Nothing in the portal therefore signals such a change to Beiersdorf during Part 2. The plan's Part 1 route (send step 3 back to step 2) is unavailable while the request sits at 'Beiersdorf: review in progress' or 'Supplier: final release'.
findings.evidence: master.md:418 says integrations have only item-level trigger events and 'no field-change trigger [owner-confirmed]'. The BASIC answers and all section answers live in P2 Answers_JSON, Editable at 'Supplier: complete section' (portal-spec.mjs:91, 101). P2 has no Beiersdorf step (portal-spec.mjs:99-103). In P1, steps 4 and 5 are 'Beiersdorf: review in progress' (an RMM step) and 'Supplier: final release' (portal-spec.mjs:76-77). Plan §6.1 line 462 re-derives only through a send-back from step 3. Plan §6.3 routed Part 2 changes through change requests, which v2 replaces with direct edits. The plan's airlock (§1) means the supplier cannot run the evaluator.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a small, supplier-safe change-notice item. It can be a new portal process, or a P4 Change Kind that skips triage. The supplier UI creates it on save whenever metadata, configuration answers or Part 2 answers change. It holds Case_Code, Section_Key, the changed field keys and the time, and lands on an RMM step 'Re-derive scope / inform departments'. This gives RMM a native task and e-mail, gives integrations an ItemCreated or ItemEntersToStep trigger, and leaves a record that cannot be changed. Without it, tell BDF that re-derivation happens at the next internal session.

findings.title: Between the last department completion and PS-11, the supplier can still change data, and the model has no route back to review
findings.claim: The built portal follows v2: answers and uploads stay editable until the supplier releases. This includes the period after every department has completed (G5), when the request already sits at 'Supplier: final release'. P1 has no route from that step back to 'Beiersdorf: review in progress'. The plan also makes G5 the point of no return and disables send-back on request steps 4 and 5. Data changed in this window would be released and frozen without review. The final PDF would still present the PS-10 completions as covering it.
findings.evidence: portal-spec.mjs:71-79 (P1 step order: step 5 leads only to End) and :101 (P2 stays editable until the supplier submits). Plan §6.1 line 482: 'G5 is the point of no return'. Plan line 451: send-back disabled on CIQP Request steps 4–5. Plan open decision 18 (line 810). BRM v2 REQ-CFG-008 and REQ-PROC-007 say editable 'until the final release in PS-11'. REQ-PROC-016 covers PS-06 to PS-10. REQ-PROC-038 says completion confirms that all assigned data was reviewed.
findings.recommended_fix: Ask BDF to choose one option. (a) Editing ends at G5: when the request enters 'Supplier: final release', the supplier UI stops offering edits, and later changes go in as change requests. This deviates from the literal 'until PS-11', and the native My Tasks screen would still allow edits, so it is a convention, not enforced. (b) A change after G5 reopens the review. This needs a P1 route from step 5 back to step 4 that does not re-fire I-1, plus reopen logic in the app. Record the answer before the custom UI is built.

findings.title: Tracing supplier edits now depends on native process-item history that has not been verified
findings.claim: v2 drops the review version and the snapshots. 'Every change is traceable' now rests entirely on the audit trail. Supplier edits overwrite one JSON blob per section, and the supplier cannot write the app's A27 audit. A27 rows are only mirrored later by internal sessions from native portal history. The per-answer by/at stamps in Answers_JSON are client-written and keep only the latest change of each answer. If native history on a portal process item does not list every update with user, time and value, and cannot be read by an internal session, intermediate changes are lost. REQ-PROC-016's audit criterion would then fail.
findings.evidence: START-HERE.md:30-32 (drop A12/A13; 'Every change is traced in A27'). Plan §4.10 line 326: 'Supplier actions cannot write here… recorded by native portal history and mirrored… by the internal session that next touches the item'. portal-spec.mjs:91 (Answers_JSON, Answers_Rev, Answers_Changed_At on one item). master.md:276 documents an item activity / audit-trail endpoint only for Board (Case) items (§3.7), and none for process items.
findings.recommended_fix: Morning test with real users. As a portal supplier, save Answers_JSON twice and change one Uploads row. Then, as a non-admin internal user, open the P2 item's history in the native UI and through the SDK or REST. Check that both changes appear with user and time, and with old and new value if available. If they do not, the change-notice item from requirements-03 must carry the changed keys and values, and becomes the audit source.

findings.title: Only the supplier can close a section, so cancellation and the no-release ending leave supplier tasks open
findings.claim: In v1, every section ended at PS-05. Under v2, every section stays open at 'Supplier: complete section' until the supplier submits it at the final release. Two endings never reach that point: a cancellation (REQ-PROC-049), and a request that ends without step 5 because Supplier_Release_Requested ≠ Yes. Both leave every section with an open supplier task and editable CIQ data. P2 has no Beiersdorf exit. The API key cannot act after Start. Only flow Admins (CIQP BDF Case Admin, CIQP Integration Service) or the initiator could withdraw, and neither has been tested on a step assigned from a field.
findings.evidence: portal-spec.mjs:99-103 (P2 steps) and :77 (the final-release step is conditional, so P1 can end without it). Plan §6.1 line 462 (v1: 'submit every in-scope section to End' at PS-05) is gone in v2. GRANTS portal-spec.mjs:161 (Admin on P2 only for Case Admin and Integration Service). master.md:257: no complete or withdraw endpoint works for a key, and reassign returns 500. Plan K-13 is still open.
findings.recommended_fix: Morning test as real users. As the non-admin RMM who created a P2 item, and as a CIQP BDF Case Admin member, withdraw a P2 item that sits at 'Supplier: complete section'. Check that the supplier's task disappears and that further supplier writes are refused. If only the admin route works, the cancellation and no-release paths need a Case Admin session, and that has to be stated together with requirements-08.

findings.title: Assigned_Contacts cannot be changed after Start, including on P1's Beiersdorf steps, while the contact list itself can
findings.claim: Supplier steps are assigned from Assigned_Contacts when the step is entered. On every portal process this field is ReadOnly after Start. That includes P1's two RMM steps, where Case_Contacts_JSON is Editable. A contact added or removed during the case therefore never reaches the 'Supplier: final release' task, which is entered from step 4. Under v2, section tasks stay open for the whole case. Removed contacts keep those open tasks, and the edit rights on CIQ answers that come with them, unless reassignment or removal from the portal role revokes them. Both are untested.
findings.evidence: Live draft of CIQP_Request_A00: Assigned_Contacts is ReadOnly at 'Beiersdorf: scope check' and 'Beiersdorf: review in progress'; Case_Contacts_JSON is Editable at both (portal-spec.mjs:74, 76). Assigned_Contacts is ReadOnly at every non-Start step on P2 and P3 in the live drafts. Spike K-04 / k04f: the field is resolved when the step is entered. master.md:257: reassign returns 500 over REST.
findings.recommended_fix: Make Assigned_Contacts Editable at both P1 Beiersdorf steps, and at the P3 review steps, so the RMM session or I-6 can refresh it before the next supplier step is entered. Morning test: as real users, check whether a send-back re-resolves the field, whether reassign works on a P2 item at its supplier step, and whether removing a user from CIQP Supplier Contact stops them acting on tasks already assigned.

findings.title: Two Beiersdorf roles hold Admin on CIQP Section, which conflicts with 'BDF roles have no edit rights on CIQ fields'
findings.claim: v2 states explicitly that BDF roles have no edit rights on CIQ fields. CIQP BDF Case Admin and CIQP Integration Service are flow Admin on CIQP Section, and the admin update route lets a process admin rewrite Answers_JSON and Uploads. The integrations I-1, I-3 and I-6 only touch P1, so the Integration Service's Admin grant on P2 has no stated purpose. The department roles also hold InitiateItems on P2. With the admin key, fields that are ReadOnly at Start were stored anyway; this has not been tested for non-admin users.
findings.evidence: GRANTS portal-spec.mjs:161; verify-report check 'CIQP Section · CIQP BDF Case Admin = A' returned 'Admin []'. master.md:249: 'PUT /process/2/{acc}/admin/{proc}/{item} # admin update (process-admin only)'. Plan §10 integration table: I-1, I-3 and I-6 act on CIQP Request only. smoke-report.json P2-answers-readonly-at-start = FAIL (Answers_JSON stored at create). BRM v2 REQ-PROC-016 acceptance criterion.
findings.recommended_fix: Remove the Integration Service's Admin grant on P2, and on P3 and P4 unless an integration needs it. Keep Case Admin's Admin on P2 only if requirements-06 shows that withdrawing needs it, and then tell BDF it is a named-admin exception. Morning test: a non-admin department user creates a P2 item that sends Answers_JSON and Uploads values; confirm they are dropped.

findings.title: The supplier can rewrite the whole query history in Thread_JSON
findings.claim: Thread_JSON holds the history of each query: Beiersdorf's questions, the supplier's answers and the decisions. It is Editable at 'Supplier: respond', so the supplier session can change or drop Beiersdorf's earlier questions and decisions. The only safeguard is native item history, which requirements-05 has not yet verified.
findings.evidence: portal-spec.mjs:123: Thread_JSON is Editable at 'Supplier: respond' (confirmed in the live P3 draft), and it is also Editable at every 'Beiersdorf review - <dept>' step (:124). Plan §4.3 line 241 describes it as 'both sides'.
findings.recommended_fix: Make Thread_JSON ReadOnly at 'Supplier: respond'. Each round, the supplier writes only Response_Kind, Response_Text and Response_Doc_Refs_JSON. The department session appends the round, together with its own decision and justification, to Thread_JSON at its review step, before it sends the query back or closes it.

findings.title: CIQP Query has no supplier-side assignee field, and its justification is optional
findings.claim: The plan says the supplier coordinator assigns work 'on sections and queries' through Supplier_Responsible_Email, but P3 was built without that field. P3's Supplier_Justification is optional, although the plan marks it as required at Start and REQ-PROC-030 lists the justification among what the supplier must see on each task.
findings.evidence: Plan §6.3 line 517 ('sets Supplier_Responsible_Email on sections and queries'). The live P3 field list has no Supplier_Responsible_Email. portal-spec.mjs:115 has TA("Supplier Justification") without required; the live draft shows Required=false; plan §4.3 line 232 says 'R Start'.
findings.recommended_fix: Add Supplier_Responsible_Email to P3, Editable at 'Supplier: respond'. Make Supplier_Justification required at Start, or enforce it as a rule in the Workbench UI.

findings.title: CIQP Change Request still accepts file uploads outside the CIQ section
findings.claim: v2 says documents are uploaded only in the relevant CIQ part and are referenced from the conversation. P4 still has a Change_Files attachment that the supplier fills at Start. Those files would sit outside the by-chapter document overview and could not be referenced by file name and upload date. Under v2, P4 is needed only for change attempts after the release and for fields Beiersdorf owns, and neither needs an upload.
findings.evidence: portal-spec.mjs:137: { name: "Change Files", type: "Attachment" }, Editable at Start (live draft). BRM v2 REQ-PROC-033 and REQ-PROC-011. 02b-…-v2-changes.md, rows REQ-PROC-016 and REQ-PROC-033.
findings.recommended_fix: Remove Change_Files from P4. Removing a field by re-PUT has been verified. The supplier uploads in the section and names the document in Proposed_Value_JSON or Change_Reason.

review.coverage_note:
Checked against BRM v2 (raw dump plus 02b), plan §3.1, §4.1–4.3, §6.1, §6.3 and §7, portal-spec.mjs, the live drafts, verify-report (379/379), smoke-report and the spike results. The live drafts are the read-only GET of /metadata/.../draft saved in the scratchpad (live/*.draft.json) at 02:50 local, after the last publish at 21:18Z. My own re-fetch was rate-limited (HTTP 429, then a Cloudflare challenge), so I did not retry. verdicts.reasoning:
Confirmed:
- portal-spec.mjs:123: 'Supplier: respond' runs only when Response_Required = "Yes".
- Live GET of the CIQP_Query_A00 draft: Response_Required is ReadOnly on all six 'Beiersdorf review - <dept>' steps.
- Smoke test P3-skip-to-dept: with No, the item goes straight from Start to the department step. So an additional-part query is in review from the moment it is raised, and the department cannot send it to a supplier step.
- P2 has one supplier step (portal-spec.mjs:99-103). BUILD-LOG says sections stay open until PS-11, so plan §6.1 line 493 (light turns amber 'once that item has ended') and §6.3 line 519 no longer work under v2.
- The live P2 field list has no due date, no responsible person and no justification field (needed by REQ-PROC-030 / REQ-ADR-001).

Overstated:
- 'The supplier has no native way to say the part is finished' is not quite right. P2 has Section_Done (Select Yes/No), Editable at 'Supplier: complete section' (portal-spec.mjs:92,101; live draft). It is only an information flag: no step change, no event, no task change.
- 'Cannot return' holds for the designed path. Another route is untested: send the query back to Start (the initiator), where Response_Required is Editable, then resubmit.
- Supplier_Reason on P2 could carry a reason, but not a due date or a responsible person.

The recommended fix needs no portal schema change: P3 already accepts Response_Required = "Yes", and the Response Kind list already has the value. So fix_kind should be a contract/plan change, not portal-spec.

- The supplier finishes the part with Response_Kind = 'Additional part completed'.
- The department accepts, or returns it with native send-back to 'Supplier: respond' (the MT-9 loop).
- The traffic light then follows the query as for any other open point.

Update plan §4.3 (the Response_Required note), §6.1 line 493 and §6.3 line 519, and tell the app session (START-HERE), because its raiseOpenPoint writes these values.

Keep Section_Done as the information flag only.

Add to MT-9 one additional-part query, to show that the supplier can read and answer it and that the department can return it.

verdicts.reasoning:
- portal-spec.mjs:71-79: step 5 leads only to End.
- portal-spec.mjs:101 and BUILD-LOG: sections stay editable until the supplier submits them at PS-11.
- Plan line 451 disables send-back on P1 steps 4-5. Line 482 makes G5 the point of no return. Open decision 18 (line 810) assumes a supplier change after G5 arrives as a change request, which v2's direct edits remove.

findings.title: I-3 and I-6 trigger on ItemExitsToStep, which may also fire on Reject or Withdraw. Cancellation and manual completion would then approve the wrong thing
findings.claim: I-3 (portal leaves "Supplier: final release") and I-6 (app leaves "Part 2 – Beiersdorf review") both trigger on ItemExitsToStep. The design itself leaves those steps by Reject or Withdraw on three paths. (1) G8 cancellation rejects CIQ Case at Part 2 or step 3. (2) RMM manual completion (REQ-PROC-045) also withdraws the portal request. (3) The supplier can natively Reject at step 5, because nothing disables it. If ItemExitsToStep fires on those exits, the integrations misfire. I-3 would write Completion_Trigger = "Supplier final release" and Approve app step 3 with no PS-11 release, which breaks REQ-PROC-045 ("without a release from PS-11 no automatic completion"). Or, after a manual completion, it would Approve whatever step is current (Overall approval). I-6, fired by a Part 2 cancellation, would copy a blank Release_Path and Approve portal step 4. Step 5 is then skipped, so the request ends Completed instead of cancelled, and the G8 cascade can no longer withdraw it.
